assessment: The observations associate course changes with affected exports but do not establish causation. Outcome payment could favor preventing selection errors or removing replacement friction. Neither proposal has established six-day feasibility or achieved the success measures.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: pay the provider a fixed fee plus a bonus for the complete next-40-export cohort meeting all three success measures. This may motivate a private, center-and-week-scoped course manifest that preserves course identity across renames and assignment changes while retaining the documented CSV.
openings.delta: Reward maintained usable exports instead of job completion. Include failed, withheld and replacement exports in the originating week's accounting so omission cannot improve the score; independently establish intended courses rather than letting the provider redefine them.
openings.prediction: Against the incumbent, fabricated reassignment and rename cases would more often match coordinator-stated intended sets without increasing checking work. Split-course cases could expose a remaining identity or isolation failure.
openings.probe: In the first coordinator sessions, establish intended sets before showing exports; compare incumbent and manifest prototypes on fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split cases. Check exact sets, center isolation and active handling time while attendance entry continues. First verify historical mapping availability and scope implementation within six engineer-days and current hosting.
assumptions: Useful historical mappings exist or can be bounded within the budget.
Coordinators can resolve intended-set disagreements without substantial recurring work.

openings.claim: If the fixed fee includes every replacement and bonus eligibility still requires the original outcome thresholds, would the provider reduce coordinator effort through immediate private self-service regeneration, or merely transfer repair work to coordinators?
openings.delta: Internalizing replacement costs might encourage faster access, but also encourage hidden manual retries or suppressed support requests. Count every attempt and all coordinator correction work.
openings.prediction: The discriminator is reduced total active handling with unchanged correctness; shorter elapsed waits alone would indicate improved availability without demonstrated handling benefit.
openings.probe: Use second sessions to compare the incumbent replacement route with a fabricated-data regeneration prototype. Measure download, checking, correction and import time separately, plus waits, retries and final course-set accuracy. Retain private processing, schema and concurrent entry; bound resource use before implementation.
assumptions: Existing export execution can be safely exposed within the remaining budget.
Session measurements approximate routine coordinator work.
